owner: codemother owns the care of this seam (ruling 2026-09-06); CC/Opus builds. The venv lay-down and the db start each keep their one existing address; bin/cairn calls them.

questions.a: Two named. (1) 'The db' is the local Postgres on 5432 and starting it is within the user's reach via sudo-relay — standing on this host; phrased as reachability with 'start' as the local remedy so a second host of the instance is not foreclosed. (2) The superclaude launcher's venv preflight can be lifted into a shared function rather than copied — standing; it is a shell block today and becomes bin/cairn's, with the launcher calling it. Neither is load-bearing beyond the build.

One point was asserted wrapped and was not: what 'it's all set up' means concretely. Now wrapped as: ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/ exists with flags/ and the instance homes the resolver symlinks into (~/.cairn/devices/<device>/0/bin/). The preflight lays that shape from class-space when missing, using the existing instance setup path, and refuses (loud, nonzero, named) if it cannot.

Consulted the lab. launchers charter's preflight has the same why (floor before anything runs); this widens its reach to the command every caller shares — a distinction to record, and the launcher keeps its own until the command's is proven. Ruling 2026-08-11 (no system-level startup) is honoured: everything here is a lazy lay-down at command time. No Law collides; Law 7 is served.

A Haiku-level builder needs: (a) the three checks in order and their remedies — venv: `~/.cairn/venv/bin/python3` exists else call the launcher's lay-down; db: `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432` (or db_domain's probe if one exists — check cairn/devices/db_domain first) else the store's start path; instance: `~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/` exists else the instance setup; (b) that bin/cairn is bash and must exec the device launcher at the end unchanged; (c) the measurement harness — copy the launchers charter's interleaved n=15 method, report median with min/max, and keep the number in the charter without a gate; (d) don't — no python startup on the happy path (that alone is ~30ms), no daemon, no cache file that could go stale. All written into the ticket's how.

watchme: none, because the floor is checked on every command by construction; the only operational signal is the happy-path cost, which the proof records and the launchers charter's what_a_launch_COSTS entry (cairn/launchers/intention+why.json) is the precedent for keeping without a gate
